title: Anthropic's record IPO draws fire from AI researchers
title_zh: Anthropic创纪录IPO，却遭AI研究者集体炮轰

image.credit: Photo by Annie Spratt on Unsplash
image.author: Annie Spratt

lead: Anthropic listed on Nasdaq on Wednesday in the largest IPO ever, raising $81.34 billion. The same day, nearly 100 AI researchers published an open letter accusing the company of hypocrisy over safety.
lead_zh: Anthropic周三登陆纳斯达克，募资813.4亿美元，创史上最大IPO纪录。同一天，近百位AI研究者发表公开信，指责该公司在安全问题上虚伪。

paragraphs: Anthropic, the company behind the Claude models, sold 980 million shares at $83 each, surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion offering in June. Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, TSMC, AMD, Broadcom and Micron agreed to buy a further $26 billion of Class N stock at the same price, bringing Anthropic's expected proceeds to about $105.4 billion. The filing discloses $900.9 billion in computing and infrastructure commitments, with $451.6 billion due by the end of 2030.

Yet the listing prompted an extraordinary backlash. The MisAnthropic Statement, signed by nearly 100 leading researchers, founders and scientists, argues that Anthropic is not a safe AI company and should not keep expanding its control over AI's future in the name of protecting humanity. Signatories range from accelerationists such as Guillaume Verdon and hacker George Hotz to safety advocates, alongside Hugging Face co-founder Thomas Wolf, xAI co-founder Igor Babuschkin and Turing Award winner Judea Pearl.

The letter targets what critics see as a contradiction at the heart of Anthropic's pitch. The prospectus promotes 'recursive self-improvement' — each Claude model helping build the next — as a core structural advantage, and says the proceeds will chiefly fund more computing power to achieve that breakthrough first. The same document warns that frontier models could concentrate power and wealth, erode trust and destabilise geopolitics, or cause large-scale harm through autonomous actions.

Anthropic's internal culture is equally paradoxical. New York Times columnist Jasmine Sun, who interviewed dozens of employees, describes young researchers who will become millionaires overnight yet remain in shared apartments, working punishing hours and pledging stock to effective altruism. Many believe a superhuman AI researcher could arrive by 2027. Critics ask why idealists who fear losing control are accelerating rather than braking, and whether any commitment to safety can be verified.

The opening bell has rung. The $900.9 billion wager, the cross-faction anger and the employees' apocalyptic anxiety will now be interrogated by quarterly earnings. The more Anthropic believes it is humanity's guardian, the more reason it has to outrun every rival.
paragraphs_zh: Claude模型背后的公司Anthropic以每股83美元发行9.8亿股，超过SpaceX今年6月约750亿美元的IPO纪录。英伟达、微软、谷歌、台积电、AMD、博通和美光同意以发行价额外认购260亿美元的N类股，使Anthropic预计募资约1054亿美元。招股书披露了9009亿美元的算力与基础设施承诺，其中4516亿美元将在2030年底前支出。

然而，此次上市引发了强烈反弹。《厌恶Anthropic声明》由近百位顶尖研究者、创始人和科学家联署，认为Anthropic并非安全的AI公司，不应以保护人类之名不断扩大对AI未来的控制权。签署者既有Guillaume Verdon和黑客George Hotz等加速主义者，也有安全派人士，还包括Hugging Face联合创始人Thomas Wolf、xAI联合创始人Igor Babuschkin和图灵奖得主Judea Pearl。
公开信直指Anthropic叙事核心的矛盾。招股书将“递归自我改进”——每一代Claude协助构建下一代——标榜为核心结构性优势，并表示募资首要用途是购买更多算力以抢先实现这一突破。但同一文件又警告，前沿模型可能集中权力与财富、侵蚀信任、破坏地缘政治稳定，或通过自主行动造成大规模伤害。
Anthropic的内部文化同样矛盾。《纽约时报》专栏作家Jasmine Sun采访了数十名员工，描绘出这样一幅图景：年轻研究员一夜之间将成为千万富翁，却仍挤在合租公寓里，高强度工作，并承诺将股票捐给有效利他主义事业。许多人相信超人类AI研究员可能在2027年到来。批评者质问：既然害怕失控，这些理想主义者为何不踩刹车反而加速？对安全的承诺又如何验证？
纳斯达克开市钟已经敲响。9009亿美元的豪赌、跨阵营的愤怒和员工的末日焦虑，今后将每季度接受财报的审视。Anthropic越相信自己肩负守护人类的使命，就越有理由跑得比所有对手更快。
